trust_decision.summary: On a cross-host or protocol-downgrade redirect, decide which request headers count as credentials and are dropped: a case-insensitive anchored RegExp built from the default list plus user-supplied options.sensitiveHeaders, each escaped by escapeRegex; an under-escaped name (containing ^ or |) never matches its own literal header, so that header is forwarded.

landing_point.why: The summary names regex escaping of sensitiveHeaders; escapeRegex is the only escaping helper and is called right at the filter construction (index.js:119).

fix_sites.entry_point: http.request/https.request/get from require('follow-redirects') (index.js:528-566) with options.sensitiveHeaders, also via the public wrap() export (index.js:709)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: No second implementation, lower-level API or wrapper builds a header filter; the only filter construction is index.js:118-120, and the other removeMatchingHeaders callers use fixed literal regexes (index.js:466, index.js:470).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no route to dismiss. The one weak candidate is a non-array sensitiveHeaders (for example a single string), which is silently replaced by [] (index.js:305-306); a solver could call that documented behaviour, since README.md:98 says names (plural, default [])

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Default credential stripping must keep its exact, case-insensitive, anchored matching. An over-broad fix (unanchored or substring matching, or treating '-'/'_' specially) would drop legitimate headers such as Authorization-Info-like or X-Sensitive-B-Extra on every cross-host redirect. Same-host and subdomain redirects must also keep the headers.

O6_input_shapes: header names already escaped before the fix: ] \ / ( ) * + ? . $

O7_producer.where: The filter is built inline in the RedirectableRequest constructor (index.js:117-120); there is no separate schema, cache or loader.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make the content-* drop on a POST-to-GET downgrade user-extensible (e.g. options.bodyHeaders) through the same escapeRegex-built filter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It mirrors the brand-new sensitiveHeaders option (commit 844c4d3) and reuses the same helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Let beforeRedirect change options.sensitiveHeaders, and rebuild _headerFilter in _sanitizeOptions through a second, differently escaped joiner.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _sanitizeOptions already re-normalises sensitiveHeaders after beforeRedirect (index.js:305-306), but the filter is never rebuilt, so a maintainer could plausibly add a rebuild there.

O9_family: Input canonicalisation / incomplete RegExp escaping causing a deny-list under-match (credential header leak on redirect)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js (>=4; CI matrix includes 24.x), npm, mocha + nyc
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.js:1535-1800 (sensitive headers on redirect, using a local express server from test/server.js)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add '|' and '^' (or '[') to the escapeRegex character class, or replace the regex with a lower-cased Set lookup; both are complete fixes.

out_of_scope_notes: The header filter is built once in the constructor (index.js:118-120) and is not rebuilt after beforeRedirect changes options (index.js:504-505); this is not part of the escaping property.
The fix still leaves '{', '}' and '-' unescaped (fix.diff:50), but '{' and '}' are not valid HTTP token characters, so Node would reject such header names anyway.
